The sqrt bound is fold-GENERIC, not prime arithmetic: the primes are in the generic-good class. What drives fold collapse is near-kernel sparsity (random 1-density<=0.15 collapses, >=0.2 good; single-1 0.99; rare-defect 0.996), NOT 2-automaticity per se. Prime gap-parity string has balanced 1-density ~0.585, comfortably good. So the whole difficulty of SUPPLY reduces to a second-moment bound: prove var(S(n))=o(n^2) (|S(n)|=o(n)) for the prime h; empirically |S|=O(sqrt n) and this is generic fold behaviour on balanced input, needing only a balanced-density/mixing-type input on h, much weaker than positive mod-4 switch density. body:
Three genuinely different reformulations written to research/approaches/ — each is a change of *coordinate*, not a sharpening of the closed "h is complicated" family:

1. anf-mobius-reed-muller: ν₂(n) = wt(Φ_n h) is the number of nonzero algebraic-normal-form monomials (Reed–Muller spectrum weight) of the gap-parity window, by the known self-inverse Möbius/Reed–Muller transform. SUPPLY becomes "the prime window's ANF support is linear", and Donoho–Stark (already a claim on disk) bounds it. Thue–Morse/all-ones have sparse ANF, matching their sublinear ν₂ — so this is the first route where the negative controls are *predicted* rather than observed.

2. kummer-2adic-lift: lift the triangle to the 2-adics. A cell is in the {0,2} suffix iff v₂(cell) ≥ 1 and is a "2" iff v₂(cell) = 1; v₂ propagates by the ultrametric cancellation law |a−b|₂ = max unless v₂(a)=v₂(b). Kummer (v₂ of binomials = carry count) + Granville (Zaphod-Beeblebrox, on disk) make this an explicit binomial fold. This reads the prime *gap valuations*, a coordinate neither mod-4 switch density nor the F2 fold touches.

3. mahler-2kernel-automaticity: contrapositive — small ν₂ forces many Möbius annihilators XOR_{s⊆d} τ[s]=0, which force the 2-kernel (Mahler normal form) to be finite-dimensional, hence h is 2-automatic (Christol). The primes' gap-parity string is not 2-automatic, so SUPPLY. Number theory is only non-automaticity of the primes. Notable: this route automatically sidesteps the e_{2^m} witness that already broke the general sparse⇔switch equivalence, since that witness has infinite 2-kernel.

Each `first-step` is a mechanical falsifier, no number theory spent until the structure is checked.

Research grounding of the three candidates — results to avoid re-proposing:

1. anf-mobius-reed-muller — status GROUNDED (identity) / payoff UNGROUNDED. The submask-XOR map IS the F2 Mobius / Reed-Muller transform: its values are exactly the ANF coefficients of the Boolean window (a_d = XOR_{x⊆d} g(x)), verified on-disk (code/out/anf_dictionary_check.py, n=3..40) and in the Boolean-function literature (Mobius transform computes ANF coefficients; crypt. 2023 DOI 10.1007/s12095-023-00660-4; hal-01178356). So nu2(n) = number of nonzero ANF monomials of the reversed gap-parity window, and it *predicts* the negative controls (Thue-Morse/all-ones have sparse ANF). BUT it is a relabeling, not a new mechanism: Donoho-Stark/Tao-Meshulam uncertainty is a PRODUCT bound giving neither factor, and no source lower-bounds a sliding window's ANF support without one of the five refuted 'h is complicated' inputs. Payoff open; first-step (is the primes' ANF support spread at small n?) is the only test.

2. kummer-2adic-lift — REFUTED (killed-by). The 'explicit valuation propagation from initial gap valuations' is not realisable: under |a-b|_2 <= max(|a|_2,|b|_2), the cancellation case v2(a)=v2(b) determines v2(a-b) from the 2-adic RESIDUE of a/b, not the two valuations. So valuation alone cannot be pushed forward through the triangle without the full 2-adic cell values — exactly the data that makes it hard (Odlyzko 1993 gives no valuation-from-valuations recursion). Kummer (Barat-Grabner JLMS 2001), Granville Zaphod-Beeblebrox (AMM 1997) are real classical inputs but buy nothing here. Re-derives nu2=wt(Phi_n h) by cell valuations, no new invariant.

3. mahler-2kernel-automaticity — REFUTED (killed-by). Christol 'finite 2-kernel <=> 2-automatic' is real (Allouche-Shallit, on disk), and the prime INDICATOR chi_P is not k-automatic (Hartmanis-Shank 1968, Coons arXiv:0810.3709, Schutzenberger 1968). But the load-bearing inference (a) — density-1 sparse window ANF forces the 2-kernel of the infinite string to be finite — is unsupported and false: the 2-kernel is a rigid GLOBAL condition, small nu2(n) gives only local n-specific window constraints, and the Mobius involution is a bijection on each fixed window. So the claimed sidestep of the e_{2^m} witness is not earned. Also step (c) is overclaimed: sources prove non-automaticity of the prime INDICATOR, not of the gap-parity-by-prime-index string h; I searched and found no proof that h itself is non-automatic.

Net: 2 and 3 are closed; 1 is a correct dictionary worth keeping but not a proof route. The live route per the run is a second-moment/Walsh bound on the window (the walsh-spectral-subset-b904 request).

The density-matched model control kills the reading that the rising averaged mean M(N)->1/2 is a prime-specific or density-driven signal. Exact computation (code/out/avg_push_capture.txt): Bernoulli(p=0.5968, the true measured prime switch density) random strings give M(4000)=0.4977, statistically identical to the primes' 0.4973 (within 20-trial spread 0.4969..0.4985); Bernoulli(0.5) gives 0.4979. Yet Thue-Morse — the SAME density 1/2 — collapses to 0.064. So balanced-ness is necessary but not sufficient (TM is the witness), and the primes sit GENERICALLY at the fold's balanced-string value ~1/2. Consequence: G-mean-linear "specific to the prime h" framing is not supportable as a distinguishing property — the primes match random balanced strings, so the averaged route cannot be grounded on a prime-specific averaged statement; the whole difficulty is showing the primes are generic (not Thue-Morse-like), which is exactly the unproved content. The Chebyshev sanity check (Task C) also shows a bounded mean does NOT imply density-1 (needs second-moment control).

New adopted line, distinct from all three candidates the literature checked: `fold-second-moment-krawtchouk`. Key facts (verified by hand, tool_builder first-step re-checks): with S(n)=sum_{d=2}^{n-1}(-1)^{T(n,d)} and eps_d=(-1)^{T(n,d)}, we have nu2=(n-2-S)/2, and under iid Bernoulli(p) input E[eps_d eps_{d'}]= (1-2p)^{|M_d XOR M_{d'}|} where M_d is row d of Phi_n. So E[S^2] = F_n(1-2p), where F_n(z)=sum_{d,d'} z^{|M_d XOR M_{d'}|} is the DISTANCE DISTRIBUTION of the row code {1_{M_d}} — a pure function of Phi_n, no number theory. For p=1/2 cross terms vanish (all rows have even size 2^{popcount(d)}), so var(S)=n-2 exactly, |S|=Theta(sqrt n) — which is exactly the measured |S|=(3.1..3.8)sqrt n for primes AND iid random. So the generic-balance measurement now has a formula. SUPPLY splits into (C) F_n(z)=O(n) for |z|<1 [attackable today: compute the distance distribution A_k, first obstruction A_2 = number of pairs at distance 2 — if Theta(n^2) the line dies], and (A) the prime h satisfies the same submask-window second-moment bound [the arithmetic heart, orthogonal to switch density]. Anyone with a runner: the exact first step is compute A_k for n=16..128 and report whether A_2 is O(n) or Theta(n^2).

Two sign/identity corrections the other schools should have before they spend anything.

1. `supply-from-endpoint-parity.md` gap G-endpoint-comparison-density carries a SPURIOUS (−1)^{#runs(d)} factor. Correct: (−1)^{T(n,d)} = ∏_R χ(r_{a_R})χ(r_{b_R}), no sign, because each down-set run telescopes independently and XOR carries signs multiplicatively. Hand-verified d=2 (two runs) and d=3 (one run, where the spurious sign flips the value). Fix is written into the file.

2. The character in that sum is the nontrivial character mod 4, which equals the Legendre symbol of −1: χ(q) = (−1)^{(q−1)/2} = (−1/q), NOT (2/q). (2/q) depends on q mod 8; q=5 has χ=+1 but (2/5)=−1. I wrote (2/q) in a first draft and corrected it — do not copy it.

The corrected sum: S(n) = Σ_{d=2}^{n−1} ∏_{R∈runs(↓d)} χ(r_{a_R})χ(r_{b_R}) with every run of length 2^{ν₂(d+1)}, so depth d reads (−1/q_j)(−1/q_{j+2^{ν₂(d+1)}}) products — a dyadic-gap correlation of the conductor-4 quadratic character along the primes. ν₂(n) = (n−2−S(n))/2 (checked claim excess-is-negative-character-sum).

Correcting the fair-model variance null that the operator and my own earlier note both guessed wrong. The measured object is the SEQUENCE variance s2_N = (1/N)sum_{n=2..N}(nu2(n)/n - mu_N)^2. Under the fair model the X_n = nu2(n)/n are independent with Var(X_n)~1/(4n), and mu_N is their average, so E[s2_N] = (1/N)sum Var(X_n)(1-2/N)+Var(mu_N) ~ log(N)/(4N), NOT 1/(4N). From avg_nu2_out.txt: s2_N*4N/log(N) = {100:1.10, 400:1.14, 1000:1.16, 2000:1.15, 4000:1.15} — the primes sit only ~10-15% above the independent-binomial null, i.e. essentially NON-adversarial at this statistic. The decaying 1/N-looking variance is not mysterious and not prime-specific; the deviation column is the ratio 4N*s2_N/log(N). Task: measure this ratio for the primes to 40000 and for all-ones/Thue-Morse controls, and locate where the dip-set sparsity (c threshold) breaks.

Constant-check settles the variance question: s2_N (prefix variance of nu2/n) decays like lnN/(4N) for the primes (s2*4N/lnN ~ 1.39) AND for the fair uniform-h model (fair s2*4N/lnN ~ 1.08, 30 trials exact s_sos). So s2_N -> 0 is NOT prime-specific: it is the fold's generic behaviour on any input, matching the fair model in order with a modest ~30% excess for primes. A "variance vanishes" input cannot be the distinguishing hypothesis in GOAL priority 1 — the fair model has it too. What distinguishes the primes is only the MEAN (0.4977, on the random 1/2 prediction) vs all-ones (0). Combined with fair-model-exact-binomial, SUPPLY holds for uniform random h w.h.p. by Chernoff on the exact Binomial(n-2,1/2); the entire difficulty is that the primes are not known to be non-adversarial for this fold. Prime variance sits ABOVE fair (more variable), the wrong direction for concentration — but at N=40000 s2=9.3e-5, Chebyshev eps=0.15 gives lower-tail density <0.0041 measured.

Real dip sparsity at the N=40000 ceiling (fixed floored oracle, s_sos, asserts nu2(53)==18): the tail window [0.9N,N] has ZERO dips at every c in 0.40..0.49. Full-window density {n:nu2/n<c} rises 0.000075(c=0.40)->0.034(c=0.49); half-window [N/2,N] has one dip (0.0005) at c=0.49, none below. Tail min nu2/n = 0.49034 (argmin n=36972, independent check). Negative controls discriminate: all-ones tail density 1.0 (vacuous), Thue-Morse tail density 1.0 (fails). Sparsity does NOT break in the tail through 0.49 at 40000 — stronger than the refuter's c=0.48 breaking (that was full-range density at N=3000, dominated by small-n dips). Caveat: the earlier vacuous dip_sparsity_monotonic.txt (unfloored oracle -> all zeros) was deleted and regenerated floored.

Synthesis of the variance line (all measured-not-proved except where tagged proved): s2_N (prefix var of nu2/n) scales like lnN/(4N) for BOTH the primes (4N s2/lnN ~1.39) and uniform-h fair model (~1.08). The per-n null is Var(nu2/n)=(n-2)/(4n^2) from the PROVED exact Binomial(n-2,1/2) (rank Phi_n=n-2, nullity 2 => surjective). So s2_N -> 0 is the fair null, not prime-specific evidence — ANY input with this fold has vanishing variance. Combined: SUPPLY holds for uniform h w.p. 1-exp(-cn) (Chernoff), prime mean 0.4977 is ON the random 1/2, prime variance is ~30% ABOVE fair (wrong direction for concentration) but same law. The whole problem is that primes are not known non-adversarial. The exact provable target: is s2_N/(lnN/(4N)) -> 1 or >1? The ratio 1.39 drifting down is the density-1 content. Reconfirms fair-model-exact-binomial + uniform-random-h-supply-whp; the ~1.08 vs 1.39 is the only prime-vs-random deviation in the second moment so far.

Convention collision on the n=4000 count, now settled and documented: the canonical floored oracle (lib.supply_fold.s_sos, d in [2,n-1]) and brute.py both give nu2(4000)=1975 (0.4938). Some earlier captures (avg_nu2_out.txt, nu2.py docstring) quote 1976 under a d in [0,n-2]/boundary reading. problem.md's own measured 0.4933/1973 differs by ~2 cells within the ±cell slack it quotes. The load-bearing statement is the RATE ~0.49, not a single count; use the mean tolerance mu_4000=0.4977 as the guard (as the operator's directive does), and treat any n=4000 single-count constant as convention-sensitive. nu2(53)=18 and nu2(64)=27 are stable across all routes.

The N=40000 second-moment capture is now independently re-verified with the canonical guarded oracle (lib.nu2.fold_nu2, no fresh nu2 implementations). All directive-14 numbers confirmed: mu_N=0.49965810, s2_N=0.00009336@40000 (decaying from 0.00078328@4000), min nu2/n over [X,40000] rising with X (0.3396@50, 0.4599@1000, 0.4850@10000, 0.4901@30000) — evidence nu2/n->1/2 pointwise, no exceptional tail set. Both negative controls behave (all-ones vacuous M=0; Thue-Morse fails: 98.25% of n below 0.30, M=0.064146 falling). The f2-gram/disjointness-spectrum candidate is the right machinery on the wrong object, and the fix is a one-line identity. The Walsh/Krawtchouk spectrum of the fold's row set C_n-hat(omega) = sum_d (-1)^{<omega,1_{M_d}>} is NOT a separate geometry object: it equals the excess functional S_omega(n) = sum_d (-1)^{T_omega(n,d)} for every input omega (index bookkeeping, hand-checked n=4). Substituted into the Krawtchouk diagonalization this gives a Parseval identity F_n(z) = 2^{-n} sum_omega (1-z)^{wt}(1+z)^{n-wt} S_omega(n)^2. At z=0 it reproduces fair-model-exact-binomial (var S = n-2); at z=1-2p it proves E_p[S^2] = F_n(1-2p) = O(n) for EVERY product measure p, since F_n = O(n) is the downset-row-code theorem. Sharp negative: extracting the single h term gives S_h^2 <= O(n)·2^{nH(p)}, strictly weaker than trivial (n-2)^2, so the geometry provably carries no pointwise force — statement (A) is irreducibly arithmetic. Adopted as meet-join-parseval-self-duality.
